result_summary: A literal zero-self source coordinate coupled to a 3D active complement with definite 2D transverse curvature has a continuous C0 output density bounded by 2^(7/4)sqrt(pi)/sqrt(beta sqrt(Delta)), provided outside-to-complement affine directions remain in that active 3-plane.

primary_sources.citation: Livshyts-Paouris-Pivovarov, On sharp bounds for marginal densities of product measures, Israel J. Math. 216 (2016), arXiv:1507.07949, Theorem 1.1
primary_sources.use: 3D orthogonal marginal density cap 2^(3/2) for cap-one product inputs

primary_sources.citation: Herry-Malicet-Poly, Regularity of laws via Dirichlet forms -- Application to quadratic forms in independent and identically distributed random variables, arXiv:2303.09488
primary_sources.use: scope comparison only; hypotheses are too narrow for the owner target

partner_result_applied.application: For Q_eps=2X1W+2epsX2Y1+2epsX3Y2+Y1^2+Y2^2, c1=c2=eps; combine with the new uniform 2^(7/4)sqrt(pi) bound.

unresolved_implication: Handle indefinite or singular transverse curvature and active complement dimension above three while retaining product provenance; separately derive a paid geometry from bare s3(A)>=1.
next_step: Replace the definite 2D slice cap by a quantitative logarithmic indefinite-slice envelope and integrate it jointly against the literal rank-one source smoother without taking a dimension-losing fiber supremum.
